problem:
A body of mass $2\,\text{kg}$ is moving in a straight line along the $x$-axis under the action of a single force $F,$ measured in Newtons.
At time $t\ge 0$ seconds, the velocity of the body is given by $v(t)=(2t-9){e}^{-2t}$ meters per second.

Calculate the time ${t}_{∗}$ at which the force acting on the body has zero magnitude. Do not round the answer.

${t}_{∗}=$

{{field-1}}  $\text{s}$
worked_solution:
According to Newton’s second law

$$
F(t)=ma(t),
$$

 
where $F(t)$ is the force, $m$ is the mass, and $a(t)$ is the acceleration. 

To find the acceleration $a(t),$ we differentiate the velocity $v(t):$

$$
\begin{aligned}a(t) & =\frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}t} \\  & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}[(2t-9){e}^{-2t}] \\  & =(2t-9)\cdot \frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}({e}^{-2t})+{e}^{-2t}\cdot \frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(2t-9) \\  & =(2t-9)(-2{e}^{-2t})+2{e}^{-2t} \\  & =(-4t+18){e}^{-2t}+2{e}^{-2t} \\  & =(-4t+20){e}^{-2t}\end{aligned}
$$

Since the mass is always positive, the force has zero magnitude when the acceleration equals zero. So, we set $a(t)=0$ and solve for $t:$

$$
\begin{aligned}(-4t+20){e}^{-2t} & =0 \\ -4t+20 & =0 \\ -4t & =-20 \\ t & =5\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the force has zero magnitude at ${t}_{∗}=5\,\text{s}.$
